items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: he's working with like a Sinatra singer, one of the singers that's taken over, and he's doing very well -- Perry Como, all those guys.

ctx.x: And the singers took over. Everything was a vocal. You had to do a vocal. And by the time you're working here with an orchestral dance band, somebody else a lot of times has got ahead of you, let's say, and he's working with like a Sinatra singer, one of the singers that's taken over, and he's doing very well -- Perry Como, all those guys. They always had nice, big bands, beautiful big orchestral sounds to work with. And you never got away from it.

They didn't come in with, you know, behind the Beatles' stuff. But that's -- I don't take anything away from that. The business as I see it was due for a rhythmic change, and although the early Latins brought the eight-to-the-bar and four-to-the-bar in, it wasn't four-to-the-bar; it was eight-to-the-bar, you know, their type of doing it, but the melding of the thing, it took a while to do.
